answer: A protocol resists Sybil attacks by admitting an identity only after stake-backed, time-spaced attestations from trusted agents. Each newcomer builds a trellis of signed relationships and must answer a random whisper challenge relayed through an earlier contact; failure breaks the claimed thread and burns its bond. A fake swarm therefore needs locked capital plus many long-lived, mutually consistent relationships, so creating thousands of convincing identities becomes expensive.
